npmos.glossary.access-list.defaultMessage: Who may open a proxy host: allowed and denied addresses and/or a login and password.

npmos.glossary.acme.defaultMessage: Free certificates issued and renewed automatically. Needs access to the internet and a domain reachable from it; optional in NPMOS.

npmos.glossary.advanced-model.defaultMessage: A larger detection model of open-appsec, uploaded as a file on WAF → Agent.

npmos.glossary.agent.defaultMessage: The open-appsec service that takes requests from nginx and decides whether to let them through. Its state is on WAF → Agent.

npmos.glossary.air-gap.defaultMessage: NPMOS works without the internet; going out (ACME, updates, hub) is an option you switch on.

npmos.glossary.audit-log.defaultMessage: The record of who changed what and when. The history of a host is taken from it.

npmos.glossary.bouncer.defaultMessage: The part that enforces CrowdSec bans: here nginx of NPMOS and the WAF agent.

npmos.glossary.ca.defaultMessage: Certificate authority: the certificate that signs others. For mTLS it is the CA of your client certificates.

npmos.glossary.confidence.defaultMessage: From what confidence a request counts as an attack in Prevent: Critical blocks the least, Medium the most.

npmos.glossary.crowdsec.defaultMessage: Detects attackers from logs and bans their addresses. In NPMOS it runs locally, without the CrowdSec console.

npmos.glossary.dead-host.defaultMessage: A domain that answers 404: it is reserved but serves nothing, or a TLS certificate is kept for it.

npmos.glossary.decision.defaultMessage: A CrowdSec verdict about an address: ban or captcha, for a set time.

npmos.glossary.detect-learn.defaultMessage: The WAF logs attacks and learns from the traffic, but lets everything through. Start here.

npmos.glossary.fail-open.defaultMessage: What happens to requests when the agent does not answer in time: they pass without inspection (fail-open) or are refused (fail-close).

npmos.glossary.hsts.defaultMessage: Tells browsers to open the site only over HTTPS for a long time. Hard to undo: enable it when HTTPS works.

npmos.glossary.mtls.defaultMessage: Mutual TLS: besides the server, the client shows a certificate. Without a certificate signed by the selected CA the host does not open (Required) or the host gets to know it (Optional).

npmos.glossary.nginx.defaultMessage: The web server inside NPMOS that accepts all traffic and serves the hosts.

npmos.glossary.open-appsec.defaultMessage: The WAF built into NPMOS: a machine-learning engine instead of signature lists. Works locally, without its cloud.

npmos.glossary.policy.defaultMessage: The settings file of the agent. NPMOS generates it from the hosts; expert fragments are added on WAF → Policy (expert).

npmos.glossary.prevent-learn.defaultMessage: The WAF blocks attacks (403) and keeps learning. Switch to it when Detect shows no false positives.

npmos.glossary.proxy-host.defaultMessage: A domain that NPMOS accepts over HTTP(S) and passes to an internal service (the upstream). WAF, mTLS and access lists are set on proxy hosts.

npmos.glossary.redirect.defaultMessage: A domain that answers with a redirect (301, 302…) to another address.

npmos.glossary.severity.defaultMessage: How dangerous an event is, in the terms of the agent. Important events are Critical and High.

npmos.glossary.stream.defaultMessage: Forwarding of a TCP and/or UDP port without HTTP: databases, SSH, games. Shown in the hosts table as :port.

npmos.glossary.subtitle.defaultMessage: Terms that the interface keeps in English, and what they mean in NPMOS.

npmos.glossary.tls.defaultMessage: Encryption of the connection between the browser and NPMOS (HTTPS). SSL is its old name.

npmos.glossary.tuning.defaultMessage: The local open-appsec services that collect what the agent learned and suggest tuning. Replace its cloud.

npmos.glossary.upstream.defaultMessage: The address and port where a host forwards requests (the Destination column). NPMOS checks that it accepts connections.

npmos.glossary.waf.defaultMessage: Web application firewall: inspects HTTP requests and blocks attacks (SQL injection, XSS…). In NPMOS it is open-appsec.

npmos.pki.install.defaultMessage: Install as a certificate of NPMplus (TLS of hosts)

npmos.pki.installed.defaultMessage: The certificate is in Certificates → TLS; hosts with it were reloaded.

npmos.pki.issue.summary.defaultMessage: Issued by {ca}; the CRL of the trust domain is checked by hosts.

npmos.pki.key-not-kept.defaultMessage: NPMOS does not keep this key: download the .p12 now, it cannot be downloaded later.

npmos.pki.key-source.csr.hint.defaultMessage: The key stays on the device; the subject is taken from the request.

npmos.pki.key-source.generate.hint.defaultMessage: NPMOS makes the key and hands it out once in a .p12 with a password.

npmos.pki.link.local.defaultMessage: The link uses the address of this GUI; set a public address of the PKI in Settings if clients cannot reach it.

npmos.pki.no-issuer.defaultMessage: There is no trust domain with a key yet. Create a root CA and a trust domain on the Certificate authorities tab.

npmos.pki.p12.compatible.hint.defaultMessage: Older macOS, iOS, Android and Windows do not import AES-256 containers. Turn off only when all clients are new.

npmos.pki.p12.password.hint.defaultMessage: Give the password separately from the file (in person, by phone, by another messenger). NPMOS does not keep it.

npmos.pki.reason.affiliationChanged.defaultMessage: Left the organization or changed role

npmos.pki.revoke-old.defaultMessage: Revoke the old certificate now (otherwise it works until it expires)

npmos.pki.revoke.text.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {The certificate stops opening hosts within a minute. This cannot be undone.} other {# certificates stop opening hosts within a minute. This cannot be undone.}}

npmos.pki.revoked-count.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# certificate revoked} other {# certificates revoked}}

npmos.pki.sans.email.hint.defaultMessage: Comma-separated; used by mail clients and some VPNs.

npmos.pki.secret.ca-key.defaultMessage: Export the key of the CA

npmos.pki.secret.ca-key.hint.defaultMessage: The key is encrypted with this password (PKCS#8, AES-256). Keep it offline: whoever has it can issue certificates your hosts trust.

npmos.pki.secret.link.hint.defaultMessage: The link opens once; then the file is removed. Send the password separately.

npmos.pki.secret.p12.hint.defaultMessage: The .p12 is made from the key NPMOS keeps and protected with this password.

npmos.pki.settings.public-url.hint.defaultMessage: Where clients and servers reach NPMOS for CRLs (written into certificates) and one-time links, e.g. a proxy host to the GUI. Empty: no CRL address in certificates, links on the address of this GUI.

npmos.pki.start.defaultMessage: Start with a root CA, then create a trust domain (intermediate CA) for each group of clients: office, partners, devices. Certificates are issued by trust domains.

npmos.pki.start.domain.defaultMessage: Create a trust domain (intermediate CA) under the root: certificates are issued by trust domains, and a host trusts the domains it needs.

npmos.pki.store-key.hint.defaultMessage: To download the .p12 again later. Without it the key is handed out only now.

npmos.pki.subtitle.defaultMessage: Own certificate authorities, client and server certificates, revocation and mTLS of hosts — without the Internet

npmos.pki.templates.hint.defaultMessage: A template fixes the trust domain, purpose, validity, key and the organization part of the subject; only the name is entered.

npmos.policy.add-to-default.defaultMessage: The exception will also be added to the default policy: it applies to every host that does not set its own exceptions.

npmos.policy.builtin-readonly.defaultMessage: A built-in object of NPMOS: it is updated with NPMOS and cannot be changed. Duplicate it to make your own.

npmos.policy.condition.hint.defaultMessage: Conditions with the same field match any of their values; different fields must all match.

npmos.policy.default.hint.defaultMessage: Applies to requests of hosts without WAF and to what a host does not set itself. Exceptions of the default policy apply to every host.

npmos.policy.default.mode-hint.defaultMessage: Usually inactive: hosts turn the WAF on in their settings.

npmos.policy.f.snortSignatures.files.defaultMessage: Files of signatures in the agent, one per line

npmos.policy.format.v1.defaultMessage: The agent gets the policy in v1beta1 (as open-appsec-npm): every exception of a rule applies.

npmos.policy.format.v2.defaultMessage: The policy uses features of v1beta2 only, so the agent gets v1beta2:

npmos.policy.import.hint.defaultMessage: A local_policy.yaml of open-appsec (v1beta1 or v1beta2) or an export of NPMOS. Objects and the default policy are imported; objects with the same name are updated, built-in ones are kept.

npmos.policy.import.policy.defaultMessage: The default policy will be replaced.

npmos.policy.import.rules.defaultMessage: Rules of hosts in the file ({count}) are not imported: hosts choose their objects in their WAF settings.

npmos.policy.kind.access_control.hint.defaultMessage: Rate limits by URI and source. Using them switches local_policy.yaml to v1beta2.

npmos.policy.kind.custom_response.hint.defaultMessage: What a blocked client gets: a code, a block page or a redirect (v1beta2).

npmos.policy.kind.exception.hint.defaultMessage: Requests the WAF lets through, drops or does not log, by source, URL, parameter, protection or country.

npmos.policy.kind.log_trigger.hint.defaultMessage: Which events the agent logs and with which details (NPMOS reads them for WAF → Events).

npmos.policy.kind.source_identifiers.hin.defaultMessage: How the agent tells clients apart: IP, X-Forwarded-For, a header, a cookie or a JWT key.

npmos.policy.kind.threat_prevention.hint.defaultMessage: What the WAF inspects and how strictly: web attacks (ML), Snort signatures; IPS, file security, schema validation and anti-bot need the Premium edition of the agent.

npmos.policy.kind.trusted_sources.hint.defaultMessage: Sources whose traffic teaches the ML model faster (learning).

npmos.policy.name.hint.defaultMessage: Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes; used in local_policy.yaml.

npmos.policy.name.invalid.defaultMessage: The name may contain lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-" and must start and end with a letter or digit.

npmos.policy.rollback-confirm.defaultMessage: Restore objects, the default policy and the objects of hosts as of version {id}? It is saved as a new version.

npmos.policy.subtitle.defaultMessage: The open-appsec policy made of objects: practices, rate limits, log triggers, responses, exceptions. Hosts use the default policy, a template or their own objects.

npmos.policy.warning.exceptions.defaultMessage: Rule {rule} has several exceptions: in v1beta2 the agent applies only the first one. Join them into one exception.

npmos.policy.warning.missing.defaultMessage: Rule {rule} refers to {name}, which does not exist (expert fragment?): the agent ignores it.

npmos.rbac.action.apply.desc.defaultMessage: Send the policy to the agent now

npmos.rbac.action.decide.desc.defaultMessage: Ban and unban addresses by hand, download blocklists

npmos.rbac.action.label.desc.defaultMessage: Mark requests as legitimate or attacks

npmos.rbac.action.view.desc.defaultMessage: See it in the interface and the API

npmos.rbac.builtin.administrator.desc.defaultMessage: Everything, including users, roles and settings.

npmos.rbac.builtin.note.defaultMessage: Permissions of built-in roles come with NPMOS and change with its updates. Only the OIDC groups can be set here; for other permissions, duplicate the role.

npmos.rbac.builtin.operator.desc.defaultMessage: Runs hosts, certificates, WAF and services; sees events and the audit log. No users, roles or settings.

npmos.rbac.builtin.security_analyst.desc.defaultMessage: Sees hosts; runs WAF policies and modes, events, learning and CrowdSec. Does not change hosts.

npmos.rbac.builtin.viewer.desc.defaultMessage: Sees hosts, certificates, WAF, events and services; changes nothing.

npmos.rbac.delete.text.defaultMessage: Delete the role {name}? {count, plural, =0 {Nobody has it.} one {# user loses its permissions.} other {# users lose its permissions.}}

npmos.rbac.hint.roles.manage.defaultMessage: Create roles and give them to users, within one's own permissions

npmos.rbac.hint.services.manage.defaultMessage: Restart services, regenerate nginx configs, download diagnostics

npmos.rbac.hint.users.manage.defaultMessage: Create, change and delete users (not administrators)

npmos.rbac.hint.waf_policy.manage.defaultMessage: Change policies, WAF modes of hosts and agent settings

npmos.rbac.not-yours.defaultMessage: You do not have this permission, so you cannot give it

npmos.rbac.oidc-groups.hint.defaultMessage: Users of these IdP groups get the role when they log in with OIDC. Comma-separated.

npmos.rbac.oidc.hint.defaultMessage: When at least one role names OIDC groups, the roles of a user who logs in with OIDC follow the groups the IdP sends. The last administrator keeps the role.

npmos.rbac.oidc.scope.defaultMessage: Ask the IdP for the groups scope

npmos.rbac.resource.crowdsec.desc.defaultMessage: Alerts, bans, blocklists, hub and settings of CrowdSec

npmos.rbac.resource.roles.desc.defaultMessage: Roles, their permissions and who has them

npmos.rbac.resource.services.desc.defaultMessage: Containers of NPMOS, their logs and restarts

npmos.rbac.resource.waf_learning.desc.defaultMessage: Labelling queue and readiness of hosts (phase 8)

npmos.rbac.resource.waf_policy.desc.defaultMessage: WAF on/off, host modes, expert policy, agent

npmos.rbac.scope.all.hint.defaultMessage: The permissions on hosts, access lists and certificates apply to all of them.

npmos.rbac.scope.own.hint.defaultMessage: Only hosts, access lists and certificates the user created.

npmos.rbac.subtitle.defaultMessage: What each role may see and do. A user can have several roles: their permissions add up.

npmos.rbac.user-roles.note.defaultMessage: Permissions of several roles add up. Without a role the user can log in but sees nothing.

npmos.services.regenerate-text.defaultMessage: The nginx configs of all enabled hosts are written again from the database, then nginx is reloaded. Use it after a failed upgrade or manual changes in /data/nginx.

npmos.services.restart-confirm.defaultMessage: Restart {service}? It is unavailable for a few seconds.

npmos.services.restart-npmos.defaultMessage: Restart {service}? The proxy and this interface are unavailable for a few seconds, the page reconnects by itself.

npmos.system.env.DEFAULT_CERT_ID.hint.defaultMessage: Answered for HTTPS requests to names no host has (otherwise a self-signed one).

npmos.system.env.DISABLE_GRAVATAR.hint.defaultMessage: Avatars of users are not loaded from gravatar.com.

npmos.system.env.DISABLE_H3_QUIC.hint.defaultMessage: UDP 443 is not served; browsers use HTTP/2.

npmos.system.env.DISABLE_HTTP.hint.defaultMessage: Only HTTPS is served. ACME HTTP-01 challenges stop working.

npmos.system.env.ENABLE_MPTCP.hint.defaultMessage: Accept MPTCP connections (the host kernel must support it).

npmos.system.env.LISTEN_PROXY_PROTOCOL_H.defaultMessage: Only behind a load balancer that sends it: direct clients are refused.
As for HTTP; needs HTTP/3 turned off.

npmos.system.env.LOGROTATIONS.hint.defaultMessage: Access and error logs of nginx, rotated daily; CrowdSec reads them.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_DISABLE_TLS12.hin.defaultMessage: Only TLS 1.3: old clients cannot connect.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_FORCE_X25519MLKEM.defaultMessage: X25519MLKEM768 only; needs TLS 1.2 off and secp curves off.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_LOAD_GEOIP2_MODUL.defaultMessage: Country of the client in nginx (needs a GeoIP2 database).

npmos.system.env.NGINX_LOAD_LDAP_MODULE..defaultMessage: Basic authentication against an LDAP directory.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_LOAD_NJS_MODULE.h.defaultMessage: JavaScript in nginx for custom configuration.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_LOAD_NTLM_MODULE..defaultMessage: Keeps NTLM connections to upstreams (Windows authentication).

npmos.system.env.NGINX_LOG_NOT_FOUND.hin.defaultMessage: 404 of missing files go to the error log too.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_QUIC_BPF.hint.defaultMessage: Routes QUIC packets to the right nginx worker; needs extra privileges on some hosts.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_TRUST_SECPR1.hint.defaultMessage: NIST curves secp256r1/secp384r1 for key exchange.

npmos.system.env.NGINX_WORKER_CONNECTION.defaultMessage: Upper limit of simultaneous connections of one nginx process.

npmos.system.env.NPMOS_CHECK_VERSION.hin.defaultMessage: Asks GitHub for new NPMOS releases.

npmos.system.env.TRUST_CLOUDFLARE.hint.defaultMessage: The real client IP is taken from Cloudflare's headers; its IP ranges are downloaded.

npmos.system.env.TZ.hint.defaultMessage: Times in logs, certificates renewal and the start scripts of the container.

npmos.system.group.external.hint.defaultMessage: NPMOS works without internet; these options make it go out.

npmos.system.group.general.hint.defaultMessage: Time zone and the certificate for unknown names.

npmos.system.group.logs.hint.defaultMessage: How long nginx logs and security events are kept.

npmos.system.group.network.hint.defaultMessage: How NPMOS listens: HTTP, HTTP/3, PROXY protocol, Cloudflare.

npmos.system.group.nginx.hint.defaultMessage: Processes, connections and optional modules of nginx.

npmos.system.group.tls.hint.defaultMessage: Protocol versions and key exchange of HTTPS.

npmos.system.pending.defaultMessage: Some settings are saved but not applied yet: NPMOS needs a restart (connections drop for a few seconds).

npmos.system.restarting.defaultMessage: NPMOS restarts to apply the settings; the panel is back in about 30 s

npmos.system.saved.defaultMessage: Saved: applied at the next restart of NPMOS

npmos.waf.agent-settings.crowdsec.hint.defaultMessage: The agent checks client IPs against the decisions (bans) of the local CrowdSec. No cloud: only decisions of this stack.

npmos.waf.agent-settings.fail-open.off.defaultMessage: Fail-close: if the agent does not answer in time or is down, requests to protected hosts are rejected (security first).

npmos.waf.agent-settings.fail-open.on.defaultMessage: If the agent does not answer in time or is down, nginx lets the request through without inspection (availability first).

npmos.waf.agent-settings.pending.defaultMessage: Saved settings are not applied yet: the agent has not restarted since.

npmos.waf.agent-settings.restart-warning.defaultMessage: The agent restarts to apply the settings (a few seconds). With fail-open on, traffic keeps flowing without inspection meanwhile; with fail-close, requests to protected hosts are rejected until the agent is back.

npmos.waf.agent-settings.saved.defaultMessage: Settings saved, the agent is restarting

npmos.waf.agent-unreachable.defaultMessage: The agent is not reachable. Check the appsec-agent service in System → Services.

npmos.waf.events.description.defaultMessage: Security log of the open-appsec agent: attacks it detected or blocked and its own events

npmos.waf.events.unavailable.defaultMessage: The agent's log directory is not readable: is the open-appsec agent running?

npmos.waf.expert.description.defaultMessage: Your own fragments of local_policy.yaml (v1beta1) on top of what NPMOS generates from the WAF settings of the hosts: exceptions, trusted sources, own practices and rules

npmos.waf.expert.example.defaultMessage: Example: accept traffic of a trusted IP on all protected hosts

npmos.waf.expert.no-diff.defaultMessage: The fragment is valid, local_policy.yaml stays the same

npmos.waf.expert.no-versions.defaultMessage: No fragments yet: the policy is generated from the WAF settings of the hosts only

npmos.waf.expert.rollback-confirm.defaultMessage: Make version {id} the current one? It is saved as a new version and applied at once.

npmos.waf.expert.rules.defaultMessage: Lists (practices, log-triggers, custom-responses, exceptions, trusted-sources, source-identifiers, policies.specific-rules): an item with the name of a generated one replaces it, others are added. policies.default: your keys replace the generated ones; exceptions listed there apply to all protected hosts.

npmos.waf.expert.saved.defaultMessage: The policy was saved and sent to the agent

npmos.waf.host-description.defaultMessage: The WAF analyses every request to this host with machine learning. Start in Detect-Learn: the model learns your normal traffic and only logs attacks; switch to Prevent-Learn when the events look right.

npmos.waf.host-policy.hint.defaultMessage: Practices, rate limits, response and exceptions of this host (WAF → Policy). Exceptions of the default policy apply too.

npmos.waf.minimum-confidence.hint.defaultMessage: High is recommended. Lower values block more, with more false positives.

npmos.waf.mode.detect-learn.hint.defaultMessage: Attacks are logged, nothing is blocked. The model keeps learning.

npmos.waf.mode.prevent-learn.hint.defaultMessage: Attacks are blocked with 403 and logged. The model keeps learning.

npmos.waf.model.description.defaultMessage: open-appsec ships with a basic model. The advanced model (open-appsec-advanced-model.tgz, downloaded separately from open-appsec) detects more attacks with fewer false positives. It is unpacked when the agent starts; the upload restarts the agent.

npmos.waf.model.uploaded.defaultMessage: Model uploaded, the agent is restarting

npmos.waf.pending-disable.defaultMessage: WAF is switched off but still active: NPMOS has to restart.

npmos.waf.pending-enable.defaultMessage: WAF is switched on but not active yet: NPMOS has to restart.

npmos.waf.policy-applied.defaultMessage: The policy was sent to the agent

npmos.waf.policy-not-sent.defaultMessage: agent did not answer, it will load the file itself

npmos.waf.policy-readonly.defaultMessage: Generated from the WAF settings of the proxy hosts; manual edits are not kept. File:

npmos.waf.restart-warning.defaultMessage: NPMOS restarts to load or unload the nginx module: the proxy and this interface are unavailable for a few seconds.

npmos.waf.restarting.defaultMessage: NPMOS is restarting, the page updates by itself…

object.delete.content.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete this {object}?

settings.default-site.description.defaultMessage: What to show when Nginx is hit with an unknown Host

settings.default-site.html.placeholder.defaultMessage: <!-- Enter your custom HTML content here -->

setup.preamble.defaultMessage: Get started by creating your admin account.

stream.description.placeholder.defaultMessage: Optional description to identify this stream
